metadata.title: Pedagogical practices and civic knowledge and engagement in Latin America: Multilevel analysis using ICCS data

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses ICCS 2016 microdata with a two-stage sampling design (schools, then students/teachers) and analyzes eighth-grade students (or ninth grade where the average age in eighth grade is <13.5 years). For student-level analyses, the authors apply a within-school student weight computed as the product of class- and student-level weight factors (WGTFAC2S × WGTADJ2S × WGTADJ3S), and for school-level analyses they apply a school weight derived from WGTFAC1 and WGTADJ1S (and teacher weights from WGTFAC1 × WGTADJ1T). They also note that multilevel ICCS analyses should use software that normalizes weights so the sum of weights equals the sample size, which is intended to preserve representativeness under the complex design. The paper does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and the modeling is multilevel (HLM8) rather than ML; therefore, replicate-weight usage is not evidenced in the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable (SCKE) is based on ICCS cognitive test scaling with five plausible values, and the paper states that all five plausible values were included in the analysis. However, the manuscript does not describe how missing questionnaire/test responses were handled (e.g., whether cases with missing covariates were excluded or whether any imputation was used). Given the use of multilevel modeling with ICCS weights, this omission limits transparency about potential selection bias from missing data.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used ICCS 2016 data from five Latin American and Caribbean countries (Chile, Colombia, Peru, Dominican Republic, Mexico) participating in the ICCS 2016 cycle. The target population is eighth-grade students (or ninth grade in countries where the average age in eighth grade is <13.5 years) and their teachers in these grades. The paper does not report additional task/module restrictions beyond the ICCS cognitive test booklet design (balanced rotated design with 45-minute completion) and does not specify explicit exclusions for missing covariates; therefore, the analytic sample is assumed to be the available ICCS student sample for these countries with the variables used in the multilevel models.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICCS 2016 (cycle 2016), civic knowledge and engagement (SCKE), students aged 13–14 (grade 8/9 depending on country)
main_findings.target_variable: Civic Knowledge and Engagement (SCKE; ICCS cognitive test, 5 plausible values)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Hierarchical linear modeling (HLM8) with null model ICC: ICC = 0.23 (χ2 (119) = 309.24, p < 0.001). Country-specific significant predictors reported as regression coefficients (b) with t-tests (p-values); no ML accuracy/R² metrics reported.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICCS 2016 the study leveraged openness in classroom discussions, civic learning at school, civic participation in the wider community, expected education level (ISCED), and home literacy resources to model Civic Knowledge and Engagement (SCKE) using five plausible values, finding that civic learning and classroom openness were associated with higher SCKE in several countries while civic participation in the wider community showed a statistically significant negative association across countries. This indicates that strengthening in-class civic learning and open classroom discussion practices may improve civic knowledge, while extracurricular/wider-community civic participation may require careful alignment with academic learning goals, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: This Heliyon study analyzes ICCS 2016 civic knowledge and engagement (SCKE) for 13–14-year-olds in five Latin American and Caribbean countries (Chile, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Mexico, Peru), using hierarchical linear modeling in HLM8. The cognitive outcome is scaled on a standardized metric (mean 500, SD 100) and modeled using five plausible values included in the analysis. The authors report that 23% of the variation in SCKE resides at the group (school) level (ICC = 0.23; χ2 (119) = 309.24, p < 0.001). Across countries, openness in classroom discussions and civic learning at school are positively associated with SCKE in multiple settings, while civic participation in the wider community is consistently negatively associated. The paper does not report ML model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC) because it uses multilevel regression rather than predictive ML, and it does not document missing-data handling, limiting transparency about selection bias.
data.null_fields_interpretation: Although the Scopus search string targets AI/ML, the manuscript does not train or evaluate any machine-learning algorithms; it performs multilevel regression (HLM) with ICCS plausible values and survey weights. Therefore, ML technique fields are intentionally left empty, and the extraction focuses on the multilevel modeling results rather than predictive ML performance.
